title: The mixed-commutator bracket is additive in its second argument
statement: Let S be an arbitrary scheme and G an arbitrary group object in schemes over S. Let Lie(G) be the dual of its identity cotangent module, with the mixed-commutator bracket defined by infBracket and transported by lieEquiv in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.Lie.Bracket. For all x,y,z in Lie(G), ⁅x, y + z⁆ = ⁅x, y⁆ + ⁅x, z⁆. There are no field, affine, smoothness, characteristic or nonemptiness hypotheses.

source.place: Original LieRing instance docstring: commutator of derivations of the structure sheaf; blueprint sk-d-tangent. Detailed coefficient argument written by Q2.

proof.text: Use the explicit invariant coefficient operator of infinitesimal right translation. Its injectivity is proved by equality of all section comorphisms, followed by restriction to the identity section, recovering the tangent point. Its identity coefficient is proved zero. Under lieEquiv, multiplication of infinitesimal points becomes addition, so the coefficient map of Lie(G) is additive.

Apply the mixed coefficient comparison to the defining equality of mixedEquiv and infBracket. This identifies the coefficient of the bracket with the commutator in the associative ring of families of additive endomorphisms of sections.
Expand A(B+C)-(B+C)A by distributivity to (AB-BA)+(AC-CA). Injectivity of the coefficient map gives the original Lie(G) equality. These calculations are checked by rw and noncomm_ring in Lean.
